headline: Sales growth outpaces margin pressure; guidance raised
summary_short: Sherwin-Williams' net sales rose 7.5% y/y to $6.79 billion in Q2 2026, with diluted EPS up 14.3% y/y to $3.43, and the company raised full-year diluted EPS guidance to $10.92-$11.32.
summary_long: Net sales grew 7.5% y/y to $6.79 billion, with all three segments — Paint Stores, Consumer Brands, and Performance Coatings — contributing growth, aided by the Suvinil acquisition. Gross margin slipped to 49.2% from 49.4% as raw-material cost inflation outpaced pricing actions, though EBITDA margin (company-stated) still expanded to 21.1% from roughly 20.0% a year ago. Diluted EPS rose 14.3% y/y to $3.43 (adjusted EPS +9.5% to $3.70) as higher sales offset increased employee costs, new-headquarters expense, and additional interest expense. The company raised full-year 2026 diluted EPS guidance to $10.92-$11.32 (adjusted: $11.80-$12.20) and returned $1.46 billion to shareholders via dividends and buybacks. Cash rose to $293.5 million from $216.9 million q/q.

drivers.explanation: Management cites 'strong second quarter results' that 'exceeded guidance on a consolidated basis and across all three reportable segments,' driven by growth investments, new account wins and pricing actions, prompting a full-year guidance raise.

Net sales increased primarily due to higher sales in all reportable segments, inclusive of the October 2025 Suvinil acquisition, plus selling-price increases and low-single-digit volume growth in Paint Stores.
Gross-profit dollars rose with revenue, but margin (49.2% vs 49.4% y/y) was pressured by raw-material cost inflation, offset only partially by pricing actions the company implemented in the quarter.
Cost of goods sold rose faster than sales, consistent with the release's cited 'moderate rise in raw material costs' pressuring gross margin.

Income before income taxes rose primarily due to higher net sales, partially offset by raw-material cost inflation, higher employee-related costs, incremental Suvinil SG&A, new-headquarters costs, and additional interest expense.
